translations.text: Eager man, will you greet with words a stranger, a wise poet? Will you question the much-travelled one about creation, and ask him to tell you about the powers of the vast created things, the living, moving powers of nature, which every day, by God's decree, bring many wonders to the generations of men?

To each of those who through wisdom can hold the whole world in his heart, a thoughtful man, it is a clear sign that long ago men, warriors firm in counsel, often recited [these things] in songs through the art of minstrelsy;
…knew how to speak rightly, so that, always asking and telling about the human race and the web of secret mysteries, and always mindful, they knew the most of all men.

therefore the man who lives with courage, a deep-minded man, should ask about hidden created things, write the craft of the word-hoard in his mind, make his heart steadfast, and think rightly about what is to come;
nor should the brave thane grow weary of this, of wisely exploring the world to the full.
Learn this teaching. I shall straight away tell you more of the Measurer's abundant power than you, wise in thought as you are, can grasp with the mind in your breast. His might is exceedingly great.
It is not within the measure of men who move on the earth that one could trace out His high work in his heart any further than the Lord grants him to understand God's own command;

But we must thank the glorious Prince for ever and ever, because the eternal King will grant us beauty in spirit, so that we may easily climb onward to the heavenly kingdom, if that is enough for us in our hearts and we are willing to keep the command of the King of heaven.
Hear now this song of praise, and fix your mind on it.

Lo, in the beginning the Father almighty, high Guardian of the treasure, created heaven and earth, the sea's wide floor, and the visible creatures, which now, in that throng, through the Lord's hand [?] and exalt the holy glory.

So he who knew how to do it well ordered all things, each in relation to the other. They all had to bear a firm, appointed course, as the Steersman commanded them, in varied measures, through the great nature.

Thus they bear forth to the world the beauty of the Lord's host and the glory of his deeds, shining praise through the long ages. They steadfastly carry out the Lord's eternal word in the original place the Lord, the pure Guardian of heaven, set for them, and they eagerly keep the boundary of the sea;
his might draws forth the candle of heaven, and the oceans with it; the Lord of life calls and leads all creatures into his own embrace alone.

So glory stands forever for him, the most fitting of all judges, who created this life for us. And this bright light comes every morning over the misty slopes, wading over the waves, wondrously adorned, and at early dawn it hastens from the east, beautiful and pleasing to the generations of men;
the brightest of fires brings light to every living being, and everyone on earth to whom the true King of victories has chosen to give the sight of eyes may enjoy it.
Then the glorious star departs with that splendour into the western sky, travelling in company, until in the evening it treads the depths of the ocean outward and calls forth the dusk;
night comes after and keeps the binding command of the holy Lord. The heaven-bright sun, shining, hastens into God's creation under the embrace of the earth, the travelling star.
Therefore no man lives who is so wise that by his own ability he can know its source, or how the gold-bright sun travels across the earth into the dark mist beneath the crush of the waters,
or which of the land-dwellers may enjoy that light after it passes over the sea.
For this reason the one who had full knowledge thus set day against night, deep against high, air against water, land against wave, flood against flood, fish against billows.
These works do not weaken, but He keeps them well; they stand firmly secured, held fast by great and mighty bonds, in the majesty by which heaven and earth were raised up.
Blessed, then, are those who dwell there; joyful is that household company. That is the greatest of hosts, a countless number of the blessed, troops of angels.
They always see their own King and look upon him with their eyes; they have enough of everything.
Those who see the King of glory in heaven lack nothing at all; for them there is feasting and joy, eternal and unceasing, as comfort for the blessed.

Therefore a man should take care to obey the Creator; let every one of the children of men give up idle desires and the fleeting joy of this life, and strive toward the bliss of grace; let him let every hostile enmity sink away with the crimes of sins, and go to the better kingdom.
